label: prf:categorical-connection-unique
title: Proof of uniqueness of categorical connections up to gauge
html:
Uniqueness up to gauge follows once we show that the difference of two connections is a derivation, hence lies in a fixed module. To that end, consider the difference \omega = \nabla_2 - \nabla_1, which is R-linear: for any a, b \in A the Leibniz rule applied to both \nabla_1 and \nabla_2 gives

  \omega(ab)
  \;=\; \nabla_2(ab) - \nabla_1(ab)
  \;=\; \bigl(\nabla_2(a)\,b + a\,\nabla_2(b)\bigr)
        - \bigl(\nabla_1(a)\,b + a\,\nabla_1(b)\bigr)
  \;=\; \omega(a)\,b + a\,\omega(b).

This shows \omega is a derivation, i.e. an element of \mathrm{Hom}_{\mathbf{C}}(A, \Omega^1(A))^{\text{Leibniz}} \cong \Omega^1(A) \otimes \mathrm{Ad}(A) via the \mathrm{Ad}(A)-twisted 1-form correspondence. Connections therefore form an affine space over this module; uniqueness is up to gauge translation within this affine structure.
